matching_table.finding: Countertops are basic/dated laminate
matching_table.note: Counters read as granite-look laminate with a rolled edge — basic/dated, as gold says. No accepted condition covers countertops and no rejected condition on this photo covers them either (the only listed condition is the flooring one). A dated/basic countertop modernization item is the sort of thing this v5 catalog plainly carries (it carries older_flooring_style and dated_lighting_fixtures), so this is billable-in-principle, hence a miss rather than out_of_catalog. Note the catalog inventory itself was not inspected (Read-only review), so the in-catalog judgement is by analogy.

matching_table.finding: Backsplash has a small-format mosaic-look finish
matching_table.note: Gold states the backsplash 'has a small-format mosaic-look finish' — a neutral description of an intact, comparatively current finish, not a deficiency. Nothing in a defect/degradation/modernization catalog would bill a serviceable recent mosaic backsplash. The pipeline in fact read it correctly as newer than the rest of the room and 2c dropped it, which is the right outcome. Not a miss.

matching_table.finding: Large open upper-cabinet niche contains an exposed unfinished wood shelf or board
matching_table.note: The open upper-cabinet bay on the right has a bare unfinished wood shelf board with a raw front edge — an incomplete/unfinished cabinetry condition, not just a styling choice. No accepted condition covers cabinetry on this photo, and no rejected condition is listed. A cabinet defect/repair item (missing door / unfinished cabinetry) is the kind of item the catalog carries, so miss_candidate rather than out_of_catalog; catalog contents were not directly inspected.

matching_table.finding: Sheet vinyl flooring is dated with wear and staining near the range
matching_table.note: older_flooring_style, accepted, disposition accepted_for_work, Terra supported ('patterned sheet-style flooring is visible and has a visually dated appearance'). Covers the dated sheet vinyl and bills its replacement. One nuance worth recording but not a separate decision: the claim text says 'flooring clean but visually outdated' whereas gold also notes wear and staining near the range, so the degradation aspect visible in the photo is not represented in the billed claim — the finding is nonetheless covered by an accepted condition.

matching_table.finding: Flush-dome ceiling lights are basic/dated
matching_table.note: Two basic flush dome fixtures are clearly present. The pipeline got all the way to a resolved item: 2c survivor cd47781a6d1735ab -> dated_lighting_fixtures (modernization). It is the one issue absent from p2e.kept_issue_ids and matches the single tier_optional_suppressed count. Per the brief, 2e suppression never costs a condition, so a condition was projected — but no accepted condition covering lighting appears in conditions_on_photo. Caveat recorded deliberately: the review-excluded oc1_f46cc039d3163f19 (appendix_misnamed, case rc_4cab6e7be02b) is not inspectable here, so if that condition turns out to be the lighting one and is accepted, this row is a matched, not a miss, and the proto case below is a duplicate of rc_4cab6e7be02b. On the evidence I can see, no accepted condition covers it.

matching_table.finding: Faucet and sink fittings are older/basic
matching_table.note: Basic chrome faucet and side fitting on a stainless drop-in sink, consistent with gold's 'older/basic'. No accepted or rejected condition on this photo touches plumbing fixtures. A dated/basic fixture modernization item is directly analogous to dated_lighting_fixtures, which this catalog carries, so miss_candidate; catalog contents not directly inspected.

matching_table.finding: Basement ceiling is covered with fiberboard panels that sag and gap (deteriorating, unfinished)
matching_table.note: Accepted ceiling_cracks_or_sagging (Terra supported) is anchored on exactly these two observations: 'Ceiling panels are sagging and deteriorated.' and 'Ceiling panels have gaps.' The photo confirms both: open joints between the ceiling boards toward the rear/right and one span visibly dropped out of plane. Clean match.

matching_table.finding: Exposed ductwork with aged/deteriorating wrap runs across the ceiling
matching_table.note: Exposed ductwork crossing the ceiling of an unfinished utility basement is normal-for-context, and nothing in the v5 catalog appears to carry a duct/duct-wrap item: the sibling modernization observations that DID survive 2c ('Older plumbing is exposed.', 'Older electrical components are exposed.') both resolved to catalog_item_id null at 2d, i.e. this family of exposed-mechanical observations has no catalog target. The one arguably billable slice is the aged/deteriorating wrap (insulation replacement or abatement), and I can see soiled banded wrap on the round runs, but I have no evidence of a catalog item for it. Hedge: if a duct-condition item does exist in v5, this flips to miss_candidate attributed to 2c, since the bullet 'Duct and utility lines are exposed near the ceiling.' reached 2c and was dropped.

matching_table.finding: Painted masonry walls show peeling paint and staining
matching_table.note: Accepted wall_scuffs_marks_or_dents (Terra supported: 'The masonry walls show visible patching and discoloration.') is anchored on 'Masonry walls show discoloration and patching.', which is the same wall-surface observation gold records as peeling paint and staining. Coverage is real, so this is a match, not a miss. Caveat for the record: the claim wording ('walls scuffs, marks, or minor dents from use') describes the wrong mechanism for whitewashed masonry with a large stain, mortar patches and thinned/flaking paint - a naming-quality issue, not a coverage gap, and the same family as the appendix_misnamed lane.

matching_table.finding: Old wood rear door is rough and weathered with gaps
matching_table.note: The old weathered wood door in the rough opening at center-right is clearly visible with gaps around the frame, and no condition on this photo touches a door - the four conditions cover ceiling, walls, floor and unfinished-space only. Doors are a standard component family in a rehab catalog (v5 already carries per-surface items like ceiling, wall and flooring wear), so I judge this billable in principle rather than normal-for-context. Residual uncertainty: retrieval is scene-group scoped and this photo is scene_group 'utility', so a door item may not be reachable here at all; if so this would be out_of_catalog rather than a miss. No rejected condition covers it.

matching_table.finding: Electrical panel is surface-mounted with exposed conduit and wiring nearby
matching_table.note: Surface-mounted panel with exposed conduit is genuinely in the photo, but this is the canonical normal-for-context unfinished-basement observation, and the pipeline itself demonstrates there is no catalog target: 'Older electrical components are exposed.' survived 2c as a modernization issue and resolved to catalog_item_id null at 2d. Consistent with the standing electrical product quarantine and the parked finding that wiring observations are true-but-unactionable for photo costing. Not a miss.

matching_table.finding: Baseboards and wall-to-floor edges are incomplete and rough in places

matching_table.finding: Ceiling fan blades show substantial scuffing and finish loss
matching_table.note: Fan blades show scuffing and finish loss. matching_table.finding: Ceiling shows a broad discolored band toward the stairwell
matching_table.note: Broad grayish discolored/patched band across the upper-right ceiling toward the stairwell - plainly visible. 2a saw it ('discoloration or rough finish near the ceiling edge/header area', plus 'Check for prior water damage'), 2b emitted two bullets for it, both survived 2c, and both then resolved to catalog_item_id null at 2d. A ceiling staining / water-damage item is the kind of thing a rehab catalog should carry, so this is a miss rather than out_of_catalog. Dedup warning for the parent: because these two issues carry null items, their projected conditions are the likely candidates for the excluded 'miss_label'/'appendix_misnamed' lanes, so this proto_case may overlap an existing case.

trip_hazard_or_unlevel_floor, accepted, from bullet 'The flooring is uneven in places.' Terra: 'Several floorboards are visibly raised and uneven relative to adjacent boards.' matching_table.note: The single narrow black stair handrail is older with dull/worn paint. 2a saw it ('The single narrow metal rail and porch guard/ironwork feel dated; replacing or refinishing them'), but 2b split that one sentence into two bullets and only the porch-guard half kept the 'dated' modifier -- that half survived into curb_appeal_upgrade while the stair-rail half went out at 2c. So the pipeline's surviving condition is about the porch guard, not the step handrail, and I do not record curb_appeal_upgrade as covering. Note the adjacency though: had curb_appeal_upgrade been routed to work rather than no_action, a porch/facade ironwork refinish would plausibly have swept the rail in.

Informational, not a Part-2 extra: this condition is accepted=false (Terra verdict 'supported', then disposition no_action / route_no_action), so it is not an accepted condition left over after matching and it is not a hallucination candidate. Recording it because the photo does support the claim -- the porch reads dated and the black iron guardrail plus decorative ironwork are plainly visible, exactly as Terra's rationale describes. Gold has no standalone 'porch/ironwork is dated' finding, so gold is mildly incomplete on the modernization reading, but the underlying objects are all in gold via g3/g7. No error case. The only accepted condition on this photo (oc1_e0539e5fbe50ad8f) was consumed by the g2 match, so there are zero genuine Part-2 extras and zero hallucination candidates here. oc1_f46cc039d3163f19 is in excluded_condition_ids and was skipped entirely (it does not appear in conditions_on_photo).
